c.tagline: Africa's Atlantic capital of cobbled streets and hilltop sea views.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used; agree the fare (often a per-zone flat rate) with the driver before departure. Shared taxis running set routes are common and cheaper than private hire.

emergency.note: Fire/rescue: 131. National Civil Protection hotline: 8001112. Medical facilities are limited; serious cases are sometimes evacuated to Portugal.

hood_landmark.Plateau: Praça Alexandre Albuquerque, Praia, Cabo Verde
hood_landmark.Achada de Santo António: Achada de Santo António, Praia, Cabo Verde
hood_landmark.Palmarejo: Igreja de São Paulo Apóstulo, Palmarejo, Praia, Cabo Verde
hood_landmark.Gamboa: Praia de Gamboa, Praia, Cabo Verde

avoid.reason: Avoid peripheral districts such as Safende, Achadinha and Vila Nova, especially after dark, due to gang-related street crime.
Watch for pickpockets in Sucupira market and on the Plateau, and skip deserted beaches or unlit streets at night.

hood_desc: The compact hilltop historic core of Praia with colonial-era buildings, the main square, a pedestrian shopping street and government offices; best for travelers who want to walk to sights, markets and transit without a car.

An upscale seaside district just below the Plateau with the city's most popular beach and promenade plus Praia's most polished mid-range and business hotels; suits visitors who want ocean views within a short walk of downtown.

A large, leafy residential and commercial neighborhood favored by expats, NGO and government workers, with supermarkets, banks and several hotels; suits longer-stay visitors wanting a quieter, local residential base.

An affluent commercial and residential zone with newer shopping centers, embassies and office towers alongside business-oriented hotels; suits business travelers and those wanting modern conveniences a short drive from the center.

A working, low-key coastal district beside Gamboa beach with fishing boats on the sand and a mix of budget guesthouses and beachfront hotels; suits budget travelers wanting an authentic beach vibe close to downtown.

water.note: Despite treated desalinated supply, aging pipes and inconsistent delivery mean bottled water is safest.

transit.pay: Public buses and shared vans (hiace/Yasa) are paid in cash to the driver or conductor in escudos; there is no rechargeable transit card. Fares are flat within the city regardless of distance ridden.
transit.hours: Buses and shared vans generally run roughly 6:00-20:00; service thins out sharply after dark, so most nighttime trips are made by taxi.
transit.note: There is no metro, tram or train; getting around is by minibus/shared van, taxi, or on foot within neighborhoods like the Plateau.

bus: Aluguer/Hiace shared vans to other towns on Santiago island
ferry: Inter-island ferries (CV Interilhas and others) from Porto da Praia to Fogo, Brava, Maio and other islands

transit.m: Public bus into city center (30-40 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% at sit-down restaurants in tourist areas is appreciated but not expected elsewhere.
